\section{Introduction}
Placeholder prose fills this paragraph so that lines break and the measure shows. A lattice
here is a finite set with two operations, and nothing in this sample depends on more than that.
We state one theorem, prove it in a line, and set one display.
\begin{theorem}
Every finite lattice has a least element.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Take the meet of all its elements.
\end{proof}
As the theorem shows, the display below is centred and numbered:
\begin{equation}
  a \wedge (b \vee c) \ge (a \wedge b) \vee (a \wedge c).
\end{equation}
The paragraph continues after the display so that the grid can be judged on the line that
follows it.
